# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

# Planning notes for mission artifacts (orchestrator, 2026-10-22)

Read this before any other mission file. It records what the owner decided after `SPEC.md` v0.2 was
written, and the readiness facts the mission is built on. Where these notes and `SPEC.md` disagree,
these notes win (owner decisions after the spec); `SPEC.md` is amended as-built at the next
integration (RULES rule 8). Where these notes are silent, `SPEC.md` is the authority.

Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` (GitHub `dctellya/droid-observatory`).
Mission branch: `mission/observatory-v1` (created from `main` at `c8524c2`; pre-mission commit `2266d3e`).
Owner: David Carbajosa Tesoro (`dct`, GitHub `dctellya`).

## Files to read for context (all in the repository)

- `SPEC.md` (v0.2): §2 mission setup, §3 milestones S, M0–M5 with named tests and acceptance
  commands, §4 versions, §5 architecture, §6 tests, §7 CI, §8 deliverables.
- `ai/RULES.md` (binding), `AGENTS.md` (operational summary), `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6

- `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md` and

- `config/observatory.example.toml`, `deny.toml`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`,
  `docs/decisions/*.md`.

## Owner decisions after SPEC v0.1 (2026-10-22), all binding

1. **Session file schema.** Droid session files carry no Droid version. The mapping version is
   selected from the Droid version recorded in the **fixture header** (`droid --version`, 0.247.0
   at capture). Token usage, model, tags and child linkage are read from the sibling
   `<session-id>.settings.json` (`tokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`,
   `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage`, `assistantActiveTimeMs`, `tags`, `model`,
   `reasoningEffort`, `interactionMode`, `autonomyLevel`). Child sessions are sibling files linked by
   `session_start.callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId`. JSONL `type` values seen: `message`,
   `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`, `session_start`; `modelId`,
   `apiProvider`, `reasoningEffort` sit on assistant messages. Decision file at S integration; SPEC
   §3 M0 / §5.2 amended as-built then.
2. **Keyring.** `keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2 (feature `keychain`,
   `set_default_store`) instead of `keyring` 4.x (fails `cargo deny`). Keychain items are generic
   passwords with service `droid-observatory/<name>` and account = the login user (`dct`), not the
   item name. Items present: `droid-observatory/github-token`, `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`.
   Decision file at S integration.
3. **DMG** only in the CI `bundle` job; local builds produce `.app` (`bundle.targets: ["app"]`).
4. **Tauri evidence.** Validators treat the Tauri window as a smoke check (process alive, `Running`
   log line, WebKit connections to port 3141, System Events lists the app). The browser surface
   (`trunk serve --port 3141` driven by `agent-browser`) is the primary interactive surface. At each
   milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked, attached to
   the report.
5. **Concurrency limits** (now SPEC §5.8 v0.2): max 3 concurrent agent-browser sessions per
   `trunk serve` (1.34–1.54 GB RSS each); `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10
   cores); all cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; `trunk serve` and
   `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns 3141; cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s,
   incremental 1.46–2.08 s; `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
6. **GitHub token** is a fine-grained **read-only** PAT (Contents, Issues, Pull requests, Actions,
   Commit statuses, Metadata; repos droid-observatory and artstudio). No Checks permission: read
   check results through Actions runs (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=`) and commit

   `merged` as detected). The write-token question stays at the M3→M4 boundary.
8. **Throttling and caps.** At a Factory usage throttle (5-hour / 7-day / monthly limits) or at a
   milestone cap, the run pauses at the point reached, usage so far is written to
   `reports/usage/`, the stall flag goes up and the owner is asked. **No silent model or
   reasoning-effort downgrade, ever** (a change is a decision file, rule 19). The M0-boundary re-cap
   of M1–M5 from measured S and M0 usage stays.

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |

| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |

### 4.1 Source trait and RawRecord

```rust
pub struct RawRecord { pub ptr: SourcePtr, pub session_id: SessionId, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* one line, no newline */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SourceKind { Jsonl, Rpc, Git, GitHub }

pub trait Source {
    fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind;
    /// Pull the next records. Returns an empty Vec when nothing new is available right now.
    /// Never blocks longer than one poll interval; never returns an error for "no data".
    fn next_batch(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>, IngestError>;
    /// True when every known file has been read to its current end (replay = attach that reached EOF, D-008).
    fn at_eof(&self) -> bool;
}
```

calling). `IngestError` (thiserror): `Io { path, source }`, `FileMoved { path }`, `TooLarge { path, mb }`.

## 9. Metrics (`core::metrics`, M5)

Time states (PRD §10.1): `enum TimeState { Active, WaitingHuman(Question|Permission|Merge), WaitingValidation,
RetryFailure, IdleQueued, IdleUnscheduled }`. `pub fn partition(events_of_feature: &[Event], end: Timestamp)
-> Vec<Interval { from, to, state }>`, contiguous and non-overlapping
(`time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()`). Active intervals `[arch decision]`: each event
with `duration` contributes `[at, at + duration]`; `duration` is set by the mapper as `tool_result.at -
tool_use.at` for tool calls and `assistant.at - previous_line.at` (same session) for model generation.
`ToolError`/`HookBlocked` intervals are `RetryFailure`; an open `QuestionAsked`/`PermissionRequested`/
green-but-unmerged gate with no active interval is `WaitingHuman`; `TaskDone` without a validator start is
`WaitingValidation`; a defined feature blocked by another's active interval is `IdleQueued`, else
`IdleUnscheduled`. The oracle (below) validates these rules.

Rework windows (`metrics::rework`): open/close pairs from PRD §10.2 (`FindingBlocking→ReworkResolved`,
`QaScenarioFailed→QaScenarioPassed` same scenario, `IntegrationConflict→IntegrationConflictResolved`,
`CheckFailed→CheckPassed` same check); overlapping windows on one feature merge; unresolved at mission end
reported with `closed_by = None`. Causes: `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
Overhead (`metrics::overhead`): orchestrator intervals before the first `FeatureDefined`, replanning not
attributable, and compaction recovery; reported as its own line; `[metrics].overhead_apportionment =
"equal"` splits it and labels the output `apportioned`. Derived (`metrics::derived`): cycle (feature,
milestone, mission, per lane), waste by the 8 SPEC §5.6 causes, bottleneck (lane/role with highest
waiting + queued; lane with highest WIP/throughput), fix loops (count of `fix` cycles).

Cost (`metrics::cost`): tokens from `UsageReported` (sidecar `tokenUsage`); credits primary when
`factoryCredits` is present; otherwise `Σ tokens × per_m / 1e6` from `config/prices/<date>.toml`
(`[metrics].price_table`); every `Cost` carries `price_table: String` (the `effective` date)
(`cost_names_the_price_table_date()`). Budget meter: `[metrics].budget` or the launch `budget_usd`.

## 3. Milestones

Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. PRD §13 counts six; the seventh is the skeleton rule 2 requires, so
the PRD count is superseded here (rule 8). A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never
shipped. The spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.

**B-010 settled: skeleton before M0, and the capture is this mission.** Rule 2 wants the thinnest
end-to-end slice first; PRD §13 wants M0 to freeze the mapping before M1–M5 are planned in detail.
Both hold because the capture needs no extra mission: the moment the owner runs the §2 command, the
orchestrator's session JSONL is growing under `~/.factory/sessions/`, and the skeleton's workers
and validators add child sessions for every role. `S` replays a snapshot of that file through a
mapper that knows nothing yet (every line is `unknown.event`, counted). `M0` snapshots the same
sessions again at `S` integration, now with all four roles present, freezes it as the fixture,
and drives the unknown count to zero. The optional B-009 pre-capture is not needed; a small
sample-repo mission (PRD §13 M0) is the fallback only if role identification cannot be established
from this mission's own files.

**Common to every milestone.**

- Tests first (rule 1): each feature begins with a red test committed in the worktree; the
  scrutiny validator checks that the red run exists in the worker's log.
- Acceptance commands are the ones in §6 and `make check`; counts are pasted, not estimated.
- Exit needs: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green
  on the push, zero blocking findings open, §9/§10 rows written, README/BACKLOG/decisions index
  updated (rule 16), `reports/usage/<m>.md` and `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` added
  (B-015), and no `unknown.event` on the capture if the milestone adds a source (rule 18).
- Must not touch: `main`, another milestone's worktree, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision,
  the shared files (§2), the ruleset on `main`.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl` is the orchestrator session; its child
  sessions live in `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.children/<session-id>.jsonl` with the
  `.settings.json` beside each. A fixture is committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` on the
  directory is clean and a reviewer has read it; raw lines may carry tool output.

Everything in `config/observatory.example.toml` as committed (`[mission]`, `[ingest]`, `[github]`,
`[intervention]`, `[metrics]`, `[telemetry]`), with these additions the mission makes, each with
its reason in the file (rule 4):

| Key | Default | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `[ingest].max_watched_sessions` | 64 | Bounds file handles and tail threads on a laptop; beyond it the newest are watched and the UI says how many are not. |
| `[ingest].max_session_file_mb` | 512 | Larger files are indexed but tail reads warn; protects memory on runaway sessions. |
| `[ingest].tail_chunk_kb` | 1024 | Read size per tail step; one chunk per poll keeps latency under 1 s at typical mission output rates. |
| `[ui].event_batch_ms` | 100 | Shell→UI flush interval (§5.1). |
| `[ui].dev_port` | 3141 | `trunk serve` port for the browser host used by validators (§6); chosen outside common dev ranges, confirmed free at planning. |
| `[store].path` | `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` | One index per user; raw lines stay where Droid wrote them. |
| `[telemetry].max_milestone_labels` | 8 | 7 named milestones of this mission plus one `overflow` value; bounds the `milestone` label for any observed mission (§5.7). |
| `[telemetry].mission_switch_min_interval_min` | 30 | The exported mission changes at most twice an hour, so two missions' series never count as active together (§5.7). |
| `[telemetry].buckets.mission_cycle_seconds` | `[3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 86400, 172800]` | Missions run hours to days. |

### 5.6 Metric definitions

By reference, not restated: time states PRD §10.1, rework windows §10.2, mission overhead §10.3,
cycle/waste/bottleneck/fix loops §10.4, cost §10.5. Closed cause lists used by the engine and the
exporter: **waste causes** `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`,
`waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled` (8);
**rework causes** `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate` (4). Mission overhead is a
separate line in the app and is not exported (reason: it belongs to no card and D-010 has no label
for it). The CSV export has one row per feature with every §10.4 measure and the price-table date.

### 5.7 Telemetry series budget (D-010, B-017)

Contract: OTLP `http/protobuf` to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp`; header
value only from the keychain item `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`; resource attributes
`service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version`; labels only from `mission`, `milestone`,
`role`, `model`, `cause`; counters and histograms only; one mission exported at a time.

| Metric | Instrument | Labels | Cardinality (worst case) | Series |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 6 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (6 + `+Inf` + `_sum` + `_count`) | 9 |
| `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 5 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (5 + 3) | 8 |
| `observatory.waste_seconds` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 milestones × 8 causes | 64 |
| `observatory.rework_windows` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 × 4 | 32 |
| `observatory.fix_loops` | counter | `mission`, `milestone` | 8 | 8 |
| `observatory.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}` | 4 counters | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 3 roles × 4 models = 12 pairs × 4 | 48 |
| `observatory.cost_usd` | counter | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 12 | 12 |
| `observatory.unknown_events` | counter | `mission` | 1 | 1 |
| **Total worst case** | | | | **182** |

Expected for this mission (7 milestones, 3 role×model pairs): 9 + 8 + 56 + 28 + 7 + 12 + 3 + 1 =
**124**. Both are strictly under 200. Why these shapes: the feature-cycle histogram carries no
`milestone` label because a histogram per milestone (7 series each) would cost 56 series for a
distribution the app already shows per card; waste and rework keep `milestone` because the budget
meter and the waste chart are read per card. Guards: the `milestone` label is bounded by
`max_milestone_labels` (the ninth and later milestones of any observed mission export as
`milestone="overflow"`); `role` is the closed `Role` enum; `model` beyond four distinct values per
mission exports as `model="other"`; the exporter refuses to start if its computed worst case for the
configured buckets and limits is not under `[telemetry].max_series`, and the test
`exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` pins the 182. Series of a previous
mission stop being written when the export target changes; `mission_switch_min_interval_min` keeps
the two sets from overlapping inside Grafana's active-series window. A `service.version` change
(release) re-keys the resource once; it is not a steady-state cost. CI telemetry stays deferred
(B-002). D-010 sized the shape at up to 6 milestones; this spec uses 8 label values because the
skeleton makes seven milestones and one `overflow` value bounds other missions. Still under 200.

### 5.8 Runtime limits

From §5.5: 64 watched sessions, 512 MB per session file before warnings, 1 MiB tail chunk,
100 ms UI batch, 500 ms JSONL poll, 30 s GitHub poll, 15 s metric export, 20 min stall threshold.
The UI holds at most the visible window of events; everything else is a store query (reason: a
mission can emit tens of thousands of lines; the board must stay at 60 fps on a laptop). The host
child process is reaped on window close (M2 test). No network access except GitHub (when a token
is present) and the OTLP gateway (when enabled); both are shown in a status bar.

`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle).
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`).
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.

### 5.9 Security

- Secrets only from the macOS keychain or the environment (rule 4): `droid-observatory/github-token`
  or `GITHUB_TOKEN` for lane 8; `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` for telemetry (no environment
  fallback in the app, D-010). Never in config, store, logs or the exported telemetry.
- Raw JSONL is rendered read-only after the B-006 scrub pass, never uploaded, never copied into the
  store (PRD §11.2); rendering read-only and the merge as the one outward write are PRD §11.3.
  Fixtures are committed only after gitleaks and a human read (§3).
- The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5): confirmation names PR number and target branch;
  the app uses the repository's allowed merge method; the action is a lane-7 event.
- Telemetry carries no session id, event id, feature id or free text (D-010); the label allow-list
  is enforced in code and by test.

## 10. Metric definitions

### 10.1 Time states

Each feature, at every instant, is in exactly one time state:

| State | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Active** | A worker, validator, or orchestrator is doing something for the feature: tool call in flight or model generating. |
| **Waiting on human** | A question or approval is open and nobody is acting (lane 7 open, lanes 2–6 idle for this feature). Sub-causes: *question*, *permission*, *waiting on merge* (checks green, policy requires a human, nobody has merged). |
| **Waiting on validation** | Work is done, validator not started. |
| **Retry and failure** | Time in tool errors, `hook.blocked`, re-runs of the same command, and conflict resolution. |
| **Idle, queued** | Feature is planned and ready but blocked behind another feature (WIP limit, dependency, no free worker). A bottleneck signal. |
| **Idle, unscheduled** | Feature exists but nothing is scheduled and nothing is blocking it. Not a bottleneck signal. |

Rework is not a separate time state. It is a window (10.2) that overlays active, retry, and waiting time.

### 10.2 Rework windows

A **rework window** opens at a blocking signal and closes at its resolution event, per signal:

| Opens | Closes |
|---|---|
| `finding.blocking` | `rework.resolved` |
| `qa.scenario.failed` | `qa.scenario.passed` for the same scenario |
| `integration.conflict` | `integration.conflict_resolved` |
| `check.failed` (mission PR) | `check.passed` for the same check |

Overlapping windows on the same feature merge into one. A window with no closing event stays open until mission end and is reported as unresolved.

- **Rework time** = active time inside rework windows.
- **First-pass active time** = active time outside any rework window.

This bounds rework so that legitimate new work after a fix is not counted as waste.

### 10.3 Mission overhead

Orchestrator time before the first `feature.defined`, replanning time not attributable to one feature, and `context.compacted` recovery belong to no card. They are reported as **mission overhead**, a separate line in lane 9, never apportioned silently. An optional explicit apportionment (equal split across features) can be switched on for comparisons and is labeled as such.

### 10.4 Derived measures

- **Cycle time** (feature) = `feature.defined` → feature's last `task.done` with validation green and integrated. **Cycle time** (milestone) = `milestone.defined` → `milestone.completed`. **Cycle time** (mission) = `intent.created` → `pr.merged` (human or policy) with CI green. Stage cycle times are computed per lane.
- **Waste** = total elapsed − first-pass active time, split by cause: waiting on human (question, permission, merge), waiting on validation, rework, retry and failure, idle queued, idle unscheduled. Mission overhead is reported next to waste, not inside it. Reported per feature, per milestone, and per role.
- **Bottleneck** = lane or role with the highest sum of waiting plus queued time across features in the window, and the lane with the highest WIP relative to its throughput.
- **Fix loops** = count of `fix` cycles per milestone and per mission.

### 10.5 Cost

- Token counts are taken from `usage.reported` events per session (input, output, cache read, cache write when available).
- If the stream reports Factory Standard Credits, credits are the primary unit.
- Otherwise cost = Σ tokens × price per model and token class, from the **price table**: a dated config file (`~/.droid-observatory/prices/<YYYY-MM-DD>.toml`). The board always shows the date of the table it used, and a mission keeps the table it started with unless the user re-prices it explicitly.
- Cost is shown next to waste so that a slow, cheap model and a fast, expensive one can be compared on the same panel.

Price table example (values illustrative, table dated):

```toml

effective = "2026-10-22"
currency = "USD"

[models."claude-fable-5.1"]
input_per_m = 0.0
output_per_m = 0.0
cache_read_per_m = 0.0
cache_write_per_m = 0.0

[models."claude-opus-5-5"]
input_per_m = 0.0
output_per_m = 0.0

[models."claude-sonnet-5-5"]

[models."claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"]
```

# D-004: Grafana Cloud over OTLP as the telemetry backend

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted for the backend and the two kinds of telemetry; attribute list, resource attributes and the `active_agents` gauge superseded by D-010

## Context

The PRD needs two kinds of telemetry: the observatory's own traces and metrics (to debug
the app) and the lane-9 mission series (cycle time, waste, tokens, cost) so they can be
charted and alerted on outside the desktop window. The owner provides a Grafana Cloud stack.

## Decision

- Export via OpenTelemetry OTLP (`http/protobuf`) to the stack's OTLP gateway. Endpoint and
  `Authorization: Basic base64(instanceId:token)` come from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` /
  `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` or the keychain entry `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`.
  Never from the repository.
- Off by default (`[telemetry].enabled = false`); the app must work fully offline.
- App telemetry: `tracing` + `tracing-opentelemetry` spans for ingest, mapping, metrics,
  control; errors as span events (no separate error tracker in v1, see B-003).
- Mission metrics (names are the contract, attributes in parentheses):
  - `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` (mission, status)
  - `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` (mission, milestone, feature)
  - `observatory.waste_seconds` (mission, milestone, feature, role, cause)
  - `observatory.rework_windows` (mission, feature, cause, resolved)
  - `observatory.fix_loops` (mission, milestone)
  - `observatory.tokens` (mission, session, role, model, class)
  - `observatory.cost` (mission, role, model, unit, price_table)
  - `observatory.active_agents` (mission, role)
- Resource attributes: `service.name=droid-observatory`, `deployment.environment`,
  `service.namespace`, `service.version`.
- CI telemetry (workflow durations, test timings) is documented only: B-002.

## Alternatives

Prometheus pull (no stable endpoint from a desktop app); Sentry for errors (second vendor;
revisit if span events prove insufficient); no export (loses the external budget meter).

## Consequences

`config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]`, `.env.example`, PRD v0.3 §11.4. GitHub
Actions secret `GRAFANA_OTLP_HEADERS` and variable `GRAFANA_OTLP_ENDPOINT` are reserved
names for B-002.

# D-010: Telemetry contract for the Grafana Cloud stack

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted (owner-provided contract; code in the telemetry milestone)

## Context

D-004 chose Grafana Cloud over OTLP and sketched metric names with a wide attribute list
(`feature`, `session`, `class`, `unit`, `price_table`, a gauge for active agents). The owner
has provisioned the stack and set the operating constraints below. Cardinality on Grafana
Cloud is billed per active series, so the attribute set is the contract that matters.

## Decision

- **Transport:** OTLP over HTTP (`http/protobuf`) to
  `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp` (`/v1/metrics`, `/v1/traces`,
  `/v1/logs`). The endpoint is not a secret and lives in `config/observatory.example.toml`.
- **Credential:** the full `Authorization=Basic …` header value is read at runtime from the
  macOS keychain item with service `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` and account = the
  current user. It is never written to config, the store or logs. If the item is missing,
  telemetry stays off and the UI says so (a visible "telemetry: off, no keychain item"
  state, not a silent failure). The environment variable `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is
  for CI only (B-002); the app does not read it.
- **Resource attributes:** `service.name=droid-observatory` and `service.version` (the
  crate version). Nothing else. D-004's `deployment.environment` and `service.namespace`
  are dropped.
- **Metric attributes (labels):** only from the set `mission`, `milestone`, `role`,
  `model`, `cause`. Never a session id, event id, feature id or free text. Anything
  that varied by `class`, `unit` or `status` in D-004 becomes part of the metric name
  (for example `observatory.tokens.input`, `observatory.cost_usd`) or is not exported.
- **Instruments:** counters and histograms only. No per-event gauges;
  `observatory.active_agents` is not exported (it stays an in-app view).
- **Series budget:** the spec states the exact metric set and the number of active series
  the app adds, computed from the label cardinalities, and keeps it **under 200**. The
  arithmetic is the spec's (B-017); the shape it must fit is: one mission exporting at a
  time, up to 6 milestones, 3 roles, up to 4 models, a closed list of waste causes, and a
  histogram costs one series per bucket plus `_sum` and `_count`, so explicit bucket
  boundaries are part of the contract.

## Alternatives

- Keep D-004's attribute list and rely on Grafana's adaptive metrics to aggregate: pays for
  the series first, then hides them; rejected.
- Export per-feature series: `feature` would be the largest cardinality by far and is
  already visible in the app; rejected by the owner.
- Read the header from the environment as a fallback in the app: one more place a secret can
  leak into a shell history or a log; rejected by the owner.

## Consequences

- D-004 stays accepted for the choice of backend and the two kinds of telemetry; its
  attribute list, resource attributes and the gauge are superseded here.
- `config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]` carries the endpoint, the keychain
  service name, the allowed label set, the series budget and the revised metric names.
- PRD v0.5 §11.4 states the contract. `.env.example` marks the OTLP variables CI-only.
- B-017: the spec session computes the series count and names the histogram buckets.

## 1. Purpose

**What it is.** A Rust desktop application (Tauri 2 shell, Leptos UI, `observatory-core` library)
that shows one Factory Mission moving through nine lanes (PRD §7): Intent, Orchestrator, Workers,
Validators-scrutiny, Validators-user-testing, Integration, Human, Outside, and Time/Waste/Cost/models.
Cards are milestones with their features inside (PRD §8); every lane entry is a view over the raw
JSONL line it came from, never a copy (PRD §11.2).

**For whom.** The mission owner who runs missions from a terminal and wants to see flow and cost;
the reviewer who opens Details and merges; the engineering lead who compares models over time
(PRD §6). Single user, local data, the user's own GitHub access.

**What it must prove.** The mission is done when all of these hold on the mission branch:

1. **Attach.** A mission started from any terminal on this machine appears on the board and every
   event of it shows within 1 s (FR-L1, FR-B6), with no control channel.
2. **Replay with a frozen mapping.** `observatory-cli replay` over the frozen capture ends with
   `unknown events: 0`, and the board renders the same capture with correct lane positions
   (FR-L2, FR-B7, rule 18).
3. **Host.** A mission launched from the app shows events within 1 s and the pause, message and
   answer controls reach the orchestrator (FR-L3, FR-H1..H4).
4. **Gate and fix loop.** Against the demo branch pair in this repository (§3 M4): a red check
   opens a `fix` cycle on the affected card, a green check with a human policy shows Merge, and
   merging from the app flips the badge (FR-G3..G8).
5. **Time, waste, cost.** Metrics recomputed from the frozen capture match the owner's reference
   spreadsheet within rounding (FR-M1..M7, PRD §10); every cost names its price-table date.
6. **The build is the first dataset.** The sessions of this mission are the capture that M0
   freezes and M5 is measured against (rule 17).

**Out of scope (explicit).** PRD §5 non-goals: planning inside the app, multi-user or server
deployment, writing to Factory's hosted API beyond what `droid` does, editing or reviewing code in
the app, CI systems other than GitHub Actions. Also out: CI telemetry to Grafana (B-002), a
dedicated error tracker (B-003), Linux and Windows bundles (macOS is the target; the devcontainer
is core-only, B-001), the app performing any merge other than the human-confirmed Merge button
(FR-G5): v1 never merges on its own. Observing a merge performed by a ruleset or a bot stays in
scope: the gate badge shows `policy-merged` on detection (FR-G6, M4). Also out: a second mapping
version for Droid releases newer than the one captured. Guard: the mapper is versioned from day
one, every `Event` carries `mapping_version`, and the unknown-event count is always visible (tray,
CLI summary, exported series), so the first Droid upgrade shows as a rising count, never as a
silently broken board. And out: migrating the backlog before the mission starts (entry 19).

**What this spec answers.** The review note `ai/prd/review-2026-10-22.md` item 5 (attach is the
primary live mode, D-008). The owner decisions logged after PRD v0.5: the telemetry contract and
series budget (D-010, B-017, §5.7), M4 on a demo branch pair in this repository instead of a
private demo repository (entry 19, B-007, §3 M4), the hybrid backlog driven by the mission
(entry 19, §8), the orchestrator model id `claude-fable-5.1` (entry 21, D-006 correction, §2),
and the backlog items the spec session owns: B-005 (§6), B-010 (§3), B-014 (§7), B-017 (§5.7).
